mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's possession is below a threshold (e.g. below 45%) AND shots produced is below season average; measure whether shots_on_target FOR as a fraction of shots FOR is suppressed relative to matches where possession is at or above average.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's shots-on-target-to-shots ratio falls as possession drops below average, with the suppression amplified when shots volume is also below average — a joint non-linear relationship rather than either observable in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's joint possession-deficit and shot-volume divergence: when Team A operates with below-average possession (recent form shows a sharp drop to 41.6% vs season average 47.2%) while simultaneously experiencing a decline in shots produced (recent 10.2 vs season 12.7), the ratio of shots-on-target produced to shots produced may compress relative to matches where possession is closer to parity. This joint relationship between possession level and shot-quality conversion (shots-on-target / shots) is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession AND shots) simultaneously to detect an interaction effect on a derived ratio; not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team B as the defending side, condition on matches where shots allowed exceeds a threshold (e.g. above 18); measure whether shots_on_target AGAINST and goals AGAINST both rise disproportionately relative to the shot-volume increase, indicating a joint amplification rather than a linear scaling.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots allowed by Team B exceeds a high threshold, goals allowed rises faster than the linear extrapolation from average shot-to-goal ratios would predict — a saturation/threshold interaction between shot volume allowed and defensive quality.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent defensive deterioration is asymmetric across shots allowed vs shots-on-target allowed: shots against have surged dramatically in recent matches (23.4 recent vs 12.5 season average) while goals against have also risen (3.0 recent vs 1.7 season), suggesting a joint relationship where the ratio of shots-on-target allowed to shots allowed (opponent shot quality) may be rising simultaneously with shot volume allowed. The interaction between opponent shot volume and opponent shot accuracy against Team B is a joint two-observable mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Involves a threshold/non-linear dependence on shots allowed jointly with shots-on-target allowed and goals allowed — three observables in a non-linear joint structure, not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition simultaneously on venue (home) AND possession above a threshold (e.g. above 48%); measure whether corner_kicks FOR is elevated beyond what either the home split alone or the possession split alone would predict, testing for a super-additive joint effect.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's corner-kick production rises with possession, and this relationship is steeper at home than away — a joint venue × possession interaction rather than either dimension independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production exhibits a strong home/away asymmetry (7.0 home vs 4.5 away, season averages) that interacts with its possession level: at home Team A generates substantially more corners and holds more possession (50.5% home vs 44.1% away). The joint relationship between venue-driven possession advantage and corner-kick production — where corners rise with possession but the venue effect on possession itself is large — creates a two-dimensional conditioning structure (venue × possession level) that predicts corner output beyond either dimension alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires two distinct conditioning dimensions simultaneously (venue AND a continuous possession threshold), not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band or the standard venue split alone.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team separately, condition on matches where fouls committed exceeds a threshold; measure whether yellow_cards FOR rises disproportionately (non-linearly) beyond the average card-per-foul rate, and test whether this threshold effect differs between Team A and Team B given their divergent recent yellow card trajectories.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's yellow cards per foul rises as fouls committed increases beyond a threshold, and this non-linear relationship is steeper for Team A than Team B — an asymmetric threshold effect across the two teams on the same joint observable pair.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetric relationship between Team A's foul-committing rate and Team B's foul-committing rate, jointly with yellow cards produced, may reveal a differential card-per-foul conversion: Team A commits more fouls (11.3 season, 11.0 recent) and accumulates more yellow cards (2.24 season, 3.0 recent) while Team B commits fewer fouls (10.0 season) with similar yellow cards (2.06 season). The joint relationship between fouls committed and yellow cards received — the card-per-foul rate — differs across the two teams and may interact with the opponent's foul rate allowed, creating an asymmetric cross-team mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Involves a non-linear (threshold) relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) measured asymmetrically across both teams simultaneously — not a single observable with one band, and not a simple mirror comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on half (first vs second) jointly for both Team A and Team B; measure whether the combined second-half goal rate (Team A FOR + Team B FOR in H2) exceeds the combined first-half rate by more than the competition baseline half-split would predict, testing for a joint amplification when both teams share the same directional half-level bias.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams independently exhibit a second-half scoring uplift, the combined second-half goal rate in their head-to-head context rises above what the competition-level half-split baseline predicts — a joint two-team within-match state mechanism.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The within-match half-level split of goals reveals a structural asymmetry for Team A: Team A concedes more in the second half (1.048 per match) than the first half (0.831), while scoring more in the second half (0.880) than the first half (0.747). This half-level scoring/conceding pattern, when jointly considered with Team B's analogous half-level split (Team B scores 0.764 in H1 and 0.921 in H2; concedes 0.787 in H1 and 0.899 in H2), creates a joint within-match state structure: both teams are second-half-weighted in both attack and defence, suggesting the second half of this specific matchup may be disproportionately goal-rich relative to the first half, beyond what either team's half-split alone would indicate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on half-level splits for both teams simultaneously and comparing against the competition baseline half-split — a within-match state structure involving two teams' directional biases at once, not a single team's observable with one band.
